sections.title: Functions, Domain, and Range
sections.content: A function maps every element in set A to a unique element in set B. The Domain is the set of all valid input values (x-values) for which the function is defined. The Range is the set of all resulting output values (y-values).

sections.title: Introduction to Limits
sections.content: A limit evaluates what value a function approaches as the input approaches a specific point. If Left Hand Limit (LHL) = Right Hand Limit (RHL) = finite value L, the limit exists. Limit of (sin x)/x as x approaches 0 is 1 (in radians).

sections.title: Continuity of a Function
sections.content: A function is continuous at x = a if LHL = RHL = f(a). Geometrically, a continuous function has no breaks, jumps, or holes in its graph at that point. Polynomials, exponentials, and sines/cosines are continuous everywhere.

sections.title: Standard Derivatives
sections.content: Differentiation measures the rate of change. Key formulas: d/dx(x^n) = nx^(n-1). d/dx(e^x) = e^x. d/dx(ln x) = 1/x. d/dx(sin x) = cos x. d/dx(cos x) = -sin x. d/dx(tan x) = sec²x.

sections.title: Rules of Differentiation
sections.content: 1) Product Rule: d/dx(uv) = u(dv/dx) + v(du/dx). 2) Quotient Rule: d/dx(u/v) = (v(du/dx) - u(dv/dx))/v². 3) Chain Rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x). The chain rule is used for composite functions.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting to apply the Chain Rule for composite functions (e.g., differentiating sin(2x) as cos(2x) instead of 2cos(2x)).
2) Checking limits only from one side.
3) Finding the domain without checking conditions like denominators ≠ 0 or square roots ≥ 0.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 establishes the calculus foundation. Master finding valid inputs (Domain), evaluating basic limits, checking continuity (no breaks), and applying basic derivative rules (Product, Quotient, Chain).

tricks.title: L'Hopital's Rule
tricks.explanation: If a limit results in 0/0 or ∞/∞ indeterminate forms, differentiate the numerator and denominator separately until the indeterminacy is removed.
tricks.example: lim (x->0) (sin x)/x = 0/0. Differentiate: cos x / 1. Apply limit: cos(0) / 1 = 1.

tricks.title: Even and Odd Functions
tricks.explanation: If f(-x) = f(x), the function is Even (symmetric about Y-axis). If f(-x) = -f(x), it is Odd (symmetric about Origin).
tricks.example: cos(x) and x² are even. sin(x) and x³ are odd.

tricks.title: Logarithmic Differentiation Trick
tricks.explanation: For functions like y = f(x)^g(x), take the natural log (ln) on both sides before differentiating to convert the power into a product.
tricks.example: y = x^x → ln y = x ln x → (1/y)(dy/dx) = x(1/x) + ln x → dy/dx = x^x(1 + ln x).

tricks.title: Periodic Function Check
tricks.explanation: If f(x+T) = f(x) for all x, T is the period. The period of sin(ax) or cos(ax) is 2π/|a|. The period of tan(ax) is π/|a|.

tricks.title: Derivative of Modulus |x|
tricks.explanation: The derivative of |x| is |x|/x (or x/|x|), valid for x ≠ 0. At x = 0, |x| is not differentiable.

tricks.title: Standard Limit: (a^x - 1)/x
tricks.explanation: Limit as x approaches 0 for (a^x - 1)/x is ln(a).
